prompt:
An instrumental chamber-jazz transition that gradually transforms rhythmic
energy into intimate stillness, connecting the supplied opening and ending
audio references.

Use the acoustic piano as the continuous musical thread. Initially retain
the opening's buoyant articulation and syncopated character. Gradually
simplify the active bass pattern into fewer, longer notes. Reduce the
density of the right-hand figures, allowing fragments of the existing
piano motif to recur with increasing space between them.

As the rhythmic activity subsides, let the muted trumpet and vibraphone
recede. Introduce a soft sustained clarinet tone and restrained viola
phrases, approaching the instrumentation and phrasing of the ending
reference. Allow the piano to become gentler and more spacious, with
rounded attacks and natural decay.

Move from an explicit swung pulse toward loosely felt, slower phrasing
without an abrupt tempo switch. Preserve harmonic continuity with the
surrounding audio; avoid introducing a separate unrelated theme.

Maintain a consistent intimate room sound and smooth perceived loudness.
Let each new element emerge while an existing element recedes, creating
one evolving passage rather than alternating between two styles.
No vocals, percussion fills, dramatic climax, fade to silence, or final
resolving cadence.

Approach the ending reference naturally. No vocals, dramatic climax, final cadence, fade to silence, or repeating-loop structure.
